transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2025-06-03
- Start: 15:00 PT
- Duration: ~46 minutes
- Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood Reliability Eng), Jenna Morales (Nimbus VP Eng), Mark Liu (Nimbus SRE), Ravi Desai (Nimbus Security), Claire Ng (Nimbus Product)

Summary:
Quick follow-up to the incident on 2025-05-28 where Nimbus saw a 6-12 minute window of elevated latencies and a small percentage of requests falling back to hosted variants. We walked through the postmortem draft, clarified timelines, root cause analysis (autoscaler threshold edge case + stale KV cache invalidation during warm restart), and agreed on mitigations and next steps.

Topics:
- Timeline and root cause
- Immediate mitigations applied and verification
- Proposed runbook + rollback plan
- Observability gaps and proposed dashboards
- Compliance/audit notes (audit logs, retention)

Action items (agreed above) and next steps.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Okay, hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll try to keep this tight. This is the postmortem follow-up for the 5/28 latency spike with Nimbus. Samir and Priya are here to go through the tech detail. Jenna, Mark, hi — do you want to kick us off with how it impacted you?

[00:30] Jenna (Nimbus VP Eng): Yeah hi, thanks Alex. So um, to summarize from our side, we saw about, I'd say 2.5x median latency for roughly ten minutes, and about maybe 4% of calls fell back to the hosted variant which has slightly different tokenization and caused a downstream mismatch for a small customer bucket. It was visible on our front-end error pages, we got a manual pager at 9:17 and then mitigation at 9:23. We're happy with the remediation speed but want to understand root cause and next steps.

[01:05] Mark (Nimbus SRE): Adding, we saw request queue depth spike, autoscaler didn't spin fast enough, and there was a KV cache invalidation event around the same time that increased cold-start tokens for some sessions.

[01:32] Samir (Redwood SE): Right, and from the Redwood side we correlated the timestamps. Two things lined up: an autoscaler threshold edge-case where bursty short-lived spikes were below the heuristic for aggressive scale-up, and a cache shard rebalancing after a background maintenance job caused some prefix misses. When combined, that increased per-request compute and pushed a few routes over the latency SLO causing smart-routing fallback to kick in.

[02:10] Priya (Redwood RE): I want to call out that our routing policy did do the fallback correctly — that's expected — but the fallback wasn't ideal because the hosted variant uses a slightly different tokenizer setting and also had a different prompt template, so there was a visible UX regression.

[02:35] Jenna: Yeah that was the main customer-facing issue. It wasn't data leakage, but it was about output format differences which caused confusion.

[03:00] Alex: On the timeline, we have the incident window 09:16–09:26, pager at 9:17, mitigation at 9:23 when Redwood increased capacity and disabled the maintenance job. Is that accurate?

[03:18] Samir: That's what our traces show. We pushed a hotfix to the autoscaler config to lower the aggressive scale threshold and temporarily increased Dedicated pool capacity. We also reverted the maintenance rebalancer that was running.

[03:40] Mark: One nuance — the autoscaler hotfix took a couple of minutes to propagate to all pools because config sync is eventual in our control plane. We should document that.

[04:00] Priya: Agreed. We're proposing a config validation step and a quicker rollback path for autoscaler config.

[04:20] Ravi (Nimbus Security): Quick Q on data retention and audit logs — did any of the fallback requests go to a different tenancy or cross-tenant routing? We want to confirm there was no data crossing.

[04:40] Samir: No, nothing crossed tenancy. The hosted variants were still bound to your account and your keys; the only difference was model variant and tokenizer. We do have audit logs for the routing events and we'll attach those to the postmortem.

[05:05] Jenna: Great, please include the audit logs — compliance will want that. Also can you include an estimate of how often this could happen given our current traffic profile?

[05:22] Priya: We ran a quick simulation on your 95th-percentile traffic. With current autoscaler heuristics, this is a low-frequency event — maybe once per quarter on similar burst patterns — but with the rebalancer running it increases the probability. So recommendation is to add a maintenance window and stronger preflight checks.

[06:00] Alex: Let's walk through the RCA bullets in the draft postmortem. Samir you want to read the primary root causes?

[06:12] Samir: Sure. Root cause one: autoscaler heuristic misclassified short high-throughput bursts as noise — the threshold uses a 60s rolling window which smoothed the spike. Root cause two: KV cache shard rebalancer triggered concurrent invalidations during a maintenance job and caused a cache warm-up penalty. Root cause three: routing fallback used a hosted variant with a non-exact match in tokenization and prompt, leading to UX regression.

[07:05] Jenna: That matches our internal notes. For the cache part, can you give more detail on the shard rebalancer? Was it doing background compaction or moving shards for balancing?

[07:25] Priya: It was a rebalance step that moves cache shards to reduce hot-spotting. The job was configured to run but we discovered it didn't check for recent traffic spikes before starting; it ran while peak traffic was expected due to a daily batch at 9am. Not great timing.

[07:50] Mark: So the combination is bad timing + smoothing window + eventual config propagation.

[08:10] Alex: For mitigations, what did we apply? Samir?

[08:18] Samir: We immediately disabled the rebalancer in your Dedicated pool, increased instance count by 20% for the short window, and changed the autoscaler aggressive threshold from 0.65 to 0.5 for burst detection. Then we monitored for 30 minutes.

[08:38] Jenna: And that resolved the latency within about two minutes of the capacity increase, yes?

[08:45] Samir: Latency started to come down within a minute and normalized within about three to four minutes after capacity.

[09:00] Priya: For longer term fixes: 1) change autoscaler to use a dual-window (10s & 60s) for burst detection, 2) rework rebalancer to have maintenance windows and preflight traffic checks, 3) align tokenizer/prompt config between hosted fallback and Dedicated variants, and 4) add a runbook step to temporarily pin routing to Dedicated during maintenance windows.

[09:40] Claire (Nimbus Product): On the tokenizer alignment — how hard is that? Can it be done quickly?

[09:50] Samir: It's a config change, mostly. The difference was an old tokenizer flag left in the hosted variant. We'll push a config sync so that fallback variants use the same tokenization and prompt template. It's low-risk but we'll validate on canary traffic first.

[10:18] Jenna: Good. Also we'd like to see a dashboard that highlights fallback rate by route and tokenizer mismatch alerts. That would help detect this earlier.

[10:32] Priya: We'll add a per-route fallback metric and an alert if fallback_rate > 1% for more than 3 mins.

[10:45] Mark: Also add an alert on queue depth and a second alert if queue depth increase coincides with KV cache invalidations.

[11:02] Alex: On the compliance side Ravi, are you satisfied with the audit artifacts we plan to provide?

[11:12] Ravi: I need the routing audit logs, and the list of tenants involved. Also timestamps and confirmation that keys were never used in another tenant context. Please include the KMS request logs for that window.

[11:30] Samir: We'll package those. Quick note: there was an internal telemetry note where a few metrics were delayed in ingestion; we'll include raw prom and the ingest timestamps.

[11:50] Jenna: Can you also include cost impact? We saw a small bump from the extra capacity during the mitigation window. We'll want a cost estimate for the increased Dedicated pool for that week in case we pursue a pre-emptive elevated buffer.

[12:10] Alex: We'll include a delta cost estimate for the temporary 20% uplift and also model a subscription buffer: e.g., 10% reserved extra capacity for burst protection.

[12:30] Samir: Quick question — do we want Redwood to temporarily enable elevated Dedicated capacity for the week following incident as a precaution?

[12:40] Jenna: We're open but need internal sign-off. Claire will coordinate and get back to Alex with approval by end of week.

[12:52] Claire: Yep, I'll coordinate with finance.

[13:05] Priya: For the runbook workshop, propose we go through the failure modes: autoscaler lag, cache rebalancer conflict, and fallback tokenization. We'll do a 60–90 minute session with your oncall and SRE. We'll also walk through our rollback checklist.

[13:25] Mark: That would be helpful; include a playbook for 'disable rebalancer' and 'manual scale-up'.

[13:36] Alex: Anything else on remediation?

[13:40] Jenna: One last ask: add a test in the preflight for scheduled maintenance that simulates a 5-minute 2x burst and ensures rebalancer doesn't run.

[13:58] Samir: We'll add that to the maintenance preflight.

[14:10] Alex: Okay last bit — timeline for deliverables: postmortem doc by Thursday 6/5, raw logs by Wednesday 6/4, runbook draft by Friday 6/6, and workshop week of 6/9. Does that line up?

[14:28] Jenna: Yes will confirm internal stakeholders for the workshop.

[14:34] Ravi: Also please make sure SOC2 control references are included, specifically control CC7 and CC9 style references for audit logs & change management.

[14:50] Priya: Noted, we'll add control references and retention windows.

[15:00] Alex: Great. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the artifacts.

[15:05] Jenna: Thanks Alex, Samir, Priya. Appreciate the quick response on the hotfix.

[15:12] Claire: Thanks all.

[15:20] End of call.

Notes: Transcription contains occasional ASR errors (e.g., 'rebalancer' sometimes 'rebalance er', 'KV cache' sometimes 'K V cache'), speaker labels approximate. Attachments referenced: postmortem-draft.docx (link), audit-logs-20250528.zip (link), autoscaler-traces-20250528.json (link), flamegraphs-20250528.svg (link).
